title: tailscaled fails to start "failed to unseal state file"
body:
### What is the issue?

Yesterday, after upgrading to 1.90.2 on Arch Linux: the tailscaled service fails to start.

The motherboard BIOS firmware was also upgraded. I can not say if tailscale was upgraded before or after the firmware, or if the firmware upgrade precipitated the tailscaled failure.

I believed initially that https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/17622 was related, but the workaround in the comments does not fix my issue.

**Things done while attempting to solve the issue:**
- The BIOS fTPM has been cleared.
- The BIOS CMOS has been cleared.
- tailscale removed and reinstalled `pacman -Runs tailscale`
- `TS_ENCRYPT_STATE=false` was added to /etc/default/tailscaled

Journal summary:

Oct 26 06:59:25 [REDACTED] tailscaled[4536]: getLocalBackend error: store.New: failed to unseal state file: failed to unseal encryption key with TPM: tpm2.Load: TPM_RC_INTEGRITY (parameter 1): integrity check failed
Oct 26 06:59:25 [REDACTED] systemd[1]: tailscaled.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I was able to solve the issue.

The Arch Linux package manager is not removing all the tailscale artifacts. To reset the tailscale state you will also need to delete the following:

`sudo rm -R /var/lib/tailscale`
`sudo rm -R /var/cache/tailscale`

You can then reinstall, and the service will start working again.

**Note:** This solution is not ideal, as it requires reinstalling and reauthenticating tailscale each time the TPM is changed.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Chiming in to say I had the same issue, which appears to be _A Thing_ with the Dell XPS 15 9560 as @participant6 mentioned in https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/17622#issuecomment-3470302281 .

Tried all the same solutions as you, and the thing that finally got Tailscale working again was clearing the cache as you described and reinstalling Tailscale. I did not need to disable encrypted state in Tailscale or reset my TPM in BIOS to get this working either!

The 9560 issue is likely related to these laptops having TPM 1.2 firmware by default, despite being equipped with TPM 2.0. A firmware upgrade *is* possible... but only on Windows 🤦

Thanks for the solution!

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
@participant4 if you're using shielded VMs in GCE, this is sort of "working as expected". Node state sealing exists to prevent copying the state file between machines (which is essentially what happens when you create an image and reuse it in a new VM).
For your setup, I'd recommend either [disabling the feature](https://tailscale.com/kb/1596/secure-node-state-storage#linux) as @participant8 described, or changing the setup to register a fresh node using auth keys on each VM instance. Or if you're feeling adventurous, try [workload identity federation](https://tailscale.com/kb/1581/workload-identity-federation) instead of auth keys ;)

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
For everyone reporting the issue: the part of the error message after `failed to unseal encryption key with TPM:` matters a lot, as it can point to very different underlying causes:
- `TPM_RC_INTEGRITY` typically means that the TPM state was reset, or that the state file was copied from one machine with a TPM to another
- `TPM_RC_LOCKOUT` means that something on the machine was failing TPM authorization checks enough to trigger a lockout. Here are [some docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/tpm/manage-tpm-lockout#about-tpm-lockout) from Microsoft that explain what this is (the lockout can happen on any OS using a TPM, it's not Windows-specific)
- there are probably other cases

```bash
# Install Tailscale client
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh

# Workaround

rm -f /var/lib/tailscale/tailscaled.state
```

comments.author: participant17
comments.body:
I have futher tested together with chatgpt and that is the conclusion
Tailscale + Synology VMM + TPM_RC_INTEGRITY (Root cause & workaround)

Environment
Synology NAS (e.g. DS1821+) with Virtual Machine Manager
Ubuntu VM
Tailscale used as subnet router / exit node

Problem
After VM stop/start or storage migration:

failed to unseal encryption key with TPM:
tpm2.Load: TPM_RC_INTEGRITY
unexpected state: NoState

Node stays unhealthy although tailscaled is running.

Root cause
Synology VMM always exposes a virtual TPM 2.0 (ACPI TPM2, MSFT0101)
TPM cannot be disabled in VMM UI
Tailscale automatically prefers TPM-backed state when TPM exists
VM hardware changes (storage move, forced shutdowns) invalidate TPM-sealed state
Flags like --encrypt-state=false do not prevent TPM usage if /dev/tpm* exists

What does NOT work
Purge/reinstall
--encrypt-state=false, TS_ENCRYPT_STATE=false
Kernel params (tpm.disable=1)
Blacklisting TPM modules
udev rules removing /dev/tpm*

Definitive workaround
Block TPM access only for tailscaled using systemd device policy:

sudo systemctl edit tailscaled

[Service]
DevicePolicy=closed
DeviceAllow=/dev/net/tun rw
Environment="FLAGS=--encrypt-state=false"
Environment="TS_ENCRYPT_STATE=false"

Then:
sudo systemctl daemon-reexec
sudo systemctl restart tailscaled
sudo rm -rf /var/lib/tailscale /var/lib/private/tailscale
sudo tailscale up

Result
tailscaled cannot access /dev/tpm*

No TPM-sealed state created

Node stays healthy across reboots, storage migration, DSM updates

Would be helpful to have a global flag which switch to the old behavior without using the TPM Module.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
1.92.5 was released today that disables the two features that use TPMs by default: state file encryption and hardware attestation keys. Once you upgrade, you no longer need to pass `--encrypt-state=false` to tailscaled to work around this.

We've observed too many issues caused by these features and the many setups where a TPM device cannot be relied on.

For the foreseeable future, features using TPMs will be opt-in only.

Sorry for the disruptions!
